scope_depth.budget_fit: Within the assigned 1,200–1,800 words and eight-URL maximum.
scope_depth.incremental_value: Compares actual block-scaled and dynamic rowwise FP8 activation representations, including metadata, decode materialization, full-path byte costs, quality gates, and the BMG API boundary. Earlier FP16/BF16 storage and native16 reports do not cover sub-16-bit encoded activation streams.
limitations: This is format and source analysis, not a Strata implementation, BMG qualification, activation-quality result, or measured speedup.
The arithmetic byte savings and transfer thresholds are correctly presented as idealized calculations that omit padding, scans, scratch, and synchronization unless explicitly counted.

overlap.prior_reports: R569/R573 and R782/R783 address 16-bit state/producer-consumer contracts and GEMM types; R825 covers direct-16 numerical screens. R828 contributes a different lossy FP8 encoding layer, scale layouts, decode boundaries, and potential transfer/storage use.
overlap.versus_round829: R828 is lossy fixed or rowwise scaling with task-quality consequences; R829 is adaptive lossless coding with exact-bit and entropy/cost questions. They share a transport/capacity setting but answer different questions.

verified_primary_claims: The pinned Transformer Engine source has an SM100-or-newer kernel guard for the inspected path.
TorchAO v0.18.0 defines Float8Tensor with qdata and scale, defaults to PerRow granularity, and exposes an explicit dequantize conversion path.

The current Intel SYCL joint_matrix page lists BMG G21/G31 XMX combinations using FP16, BF16, and integer types; its matrix_type enum does not include FP8. This is an API support table, not a silicon audit.

corrections.finding: The Intel source URL targets the mutable sycl branch. The report records its retrieval date but not an immutable Intel LLVM revision.
corrections.action_before_reuse: Record the exact source commit before relying on the BMG support table for a later decision.

source_review.performance_claims: No unsupported performance claim found. Storage ratios and break-even figures are transparent arithmetic models; no BMG or Strata throughput is asserted.
source_review.provenance: Transformer Engine and TorchAO source versions are pinned and licenses are identified. No implementation is proposed for reuse.

retrieval.reason: The active path stores/consumes BF16 native16 values and is resolving QSA integration and model correctness; the report studies lossy FP8 encoding and does not validate that path.
retrieval.future_trigger: A measured Strata producer-consumer seam is shown to be limited by activation-transfer time or live-memory capacity, and its exact tensor format, shape, and layout are recorded.

scope_depth.budget_fit: Within the assigned 1,200–1,800 words and eight-URL maximum.
scope_depth.incremental_value: Compares a floating-point predictor/bit-plane codec and a multi-byte LZSS GPU pipeline, including exactness limits, output metadata, scan passes, scratch/lifetime, chunk access, data sensitivity, and a serial-versus-overlapped 6 GB/s transfer model. This is distinct from lossy R828 and CPU predecode R595.
limitations: Neither paper measures neural activation/state streams, FP16/BF16 model tensors, Intel BMG, or the assumed 6 GB/s link.
Falcon's special-value bit-preservation boundary remains unresolved; the report correctly treats its published floating-point results as workload-specific.

overlap.prior_reports: R595 concerns CPU predecode and R661 covers external lossy residual-storage quality; neither compares GPU lossless floating-stream codec passes and scratch. R828 covers scale-based lossy storage and quantization quality, not bit-preserving compression.
overlap.versus_round828: Nonduplicate: lossless coding preserves all input bits when supported, while R828 reduces precision and needs numerical/task-quality validation.

verified_primary_claims: Falcon v2 reports mean compressed/raw ratio 0.299 and mean compression/decompression throughput 10.82/12.32 GB/s on the paper's 12 datasets; its setup names RTX 5080, CUDA 12.9, and driver 575.51.03.

GPULZ v2 reports 29.00 GB/s compression for the cited A100 Hurricane configuration and mean decompression throughput of 29.1 GB/s on A100 and 16.4 GB/s on A4000; these are scientific/database workloads, not activations.
The cited nvCOMP C API documents Bitcomp's 1<<24-byte maximum uncompressed chunk, recommends smaller chunks such as 64 KiB for decompression performance, and lists lossless FP16/FP32/FP64 support.

corrections.finding: The report's GPULZ allocation/pass audit cites the mutable GitHub main branch without a commit or source snapshot hash. The approximately 4N peak-allocation conclusion is derived from that code, not established by the paper alone.
corrections.action_before_reuse: Pin the exact GPULZ revision or archive and hash the inspected source before using the code-specific allocation/lifetime details in a later decision.

corrections.finding: The Falcon artifact repository also lacks an immutable revision and identified software license; the report explicitly withholds implementation reuse.

source_review.performance_claims: Published rates are attributed to their papers and hardware. The report distinguishes GPU-only codec rates from PCIe-inclusive path time and labels the 6 GB/s break-even arithmetic illustrative; no activation compressibility or BMG speed is inferred.
source_review.provenance: Paper versions are pinned; the no-reuse boundary is appropriate. GPULZ code-derived claims require the correction above before reuse.

retrieval.reason: The active BF16 native16/QSA build has no supplied transfer or capacity bottleneck that could justify a lossless codec, and lossless compression would not establish model correctness for that build.
retrieval.future_trigger: A closed, owned profile names a tensor stream whose PCIe transfer or live allocation is material and records exact shape, byte count, producer/consumer dependency, and whether raw storage can be released.

cross_report_and_current_work.comparison: R828 is lossy block-scaled activation storage; R829 is lossless data-dependent compression. They are complementary and must not be collapsed into a generic 'under-16-bit transport' recommendation.
cross_report_and_current_work.immediate_model_or_build_correctness_rel: None of the reviewed sections establishes correctness, performance, or compatibility for the active BF16 native16 QSA build. Do not retrieve either collection body for that work absent a concrete FP8/storage or compression question.
cross_report_and_current_work.primary_source_verification: Official/paper primary sources were checked for the claims listed above. This review did not independently fetch/hash the mutable GPULZ source or re-run any experiment.
